label: text
text: Mr. Wood's first case was that of Mak Sum, charged with robbery on April 15, 1923, at Wong Nei Cheong Village. In the course of her evidence the wife of the robbed man accused the prisoner of having forced into her husband's mouth some poison which had caused his death about twelve days later, but the Crown Solicitor, Mr. Whyte Smith, said that there was some sort of suggestion that the remedies which the man had used had aggravated the injuries.

label: text
text: The most striking feature of to-day's Criminal Sessions was the heavy penalty imposed by Mr. J. R. Wood, the new Puisine Judge, on a man convicted of participation in a two years old robbery.

label: text
text: Although two years had elapsed between the time of the robbery and the arrest of the prisoner, the woman had had no difficulty in picking the man out from thirteen others at the police station. Questioned by Mr. Justice Wood she said that she would only be able to recognise the other men who took part in the robbery "partly per cent," this man she recognised "fully per cent," because he was the one who had tied her husband up. The others had not shown their forms.

label: text
text: The defendant pleaded not guilty this morning but in previous statements he had confessed to participation in the robbery. At the Magistracy he had stated that he had been arrested by a police-man who had told him that he was going to get him employment on a Government launch. This policeman had told him that unless he confessed he would be beaten to death.

label: text
text: Child stealing formed the subject of the next charge, defendant being Tam Wing Mr. Whyte Smith said that a boy had been confided to the care of a relative in Hongkong who was a tailor and to whom he was apprenticed. He disappeared on February 27 and suspicion fell on the defendant who was the adopted son of the tailor and had taken the boy out to tea on several occasions. On being questioned by the mother of the boy the defendant said "you need not be afraid, I can recover him." At the police station he had stated that he and another man had taken the boy to Macao where they had received $25 each from a "dealer in children." The boy had not been seen by his relatives since.

label: text
text: The jury found defendant guilty and Mr. Justiçe Wood sentenced him to ten years' hard labour and twelve strokes of the "cat."

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: Mr. H. E. Hollands informed the China Mail this morning, in response to inquiries, that the Committee has been working to get a side together for about a month. Many of the members of the team had been granted leave and, full particulars would be available, he hoped, in the course of the next few days.

label: text
text: Others of the last Hongkong team who have been asked if they can go include A. C. I. Bowker, Pay, Lieut. Com. Hargreaves, R.N. C.Q.M.S. Stripp, East Surrey Regt., and A. W. Ramsay of the Kowloon Cricket Club.

label: text
text: Shanghai may have a chance of retrieving the “Ashes” as there is a possibility of Hongkong sending up an interport cricket team, leaving on May 8 or 9.

label: text
text: The Rev. E. K. Quick, with his ripe experience, has been asked to be captain. He justified his being sent in to put first in the last series played here and his right-handed slow bowling brought about a separation whenever the first line of attack looked like being beaten.

label: text
text: Owing to the all-important question of leave it is hardly to be expected that the strongest team will be available. Still, according to the latest information, several of the team which defeated Singapore and Shanghai, in Hongkong, at the beginning of this season, are being discussed. What with the usual glorious uncertainty and the memory of Hongkong's victory in Shanghai the year before last, it would be decidedly rash to make any predictions.

label: text
text: KOWLOON CITY ROBBERY ARRESTS.

label: text
text: The armed robbery in which six men secured a haul of properly valued at $525 from a hut at To Koo Ling village in the Kowloon City district provided a further development when another two arrests were made during the week-end.

label: text
text: TWO MORE MEN IN CUSTODY:

label: text
text: On the gang entering the hut at 9 p.m. last Monday, a little boy slipped away unobserved and gave timely information at the Police Station. The police quickly turned out at the hut, but found that the robbers had got away with the haul. Later, they came upon two men hiding under an embankment and they were both arrested after a chase, one of them having to be shot in the back before he surrendered.

label: text
text: The wounded man is still in hospital, but his confederate, who had a dagger in his possession, was formally charged before Mr. E. W. Hamilton at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning, when he was remanded until Friday.

label: text
text: The two men arrested subsequently will be charged before the Magistrate in due course.

Another disadvantage is the increasing discount on Canton subsidiary silver coins, in which piecegoods are sold in the interior. This factor is tantamount to adverse exchange.
It was decided to approach the Hongkong General Chamber of Commerce for assistance. A letter was to be addressed to the Chamber to-day asking for (1) the extension of the delivery period of four months by an additional six months (2) and the waiving (by the importing hongs) of the interest which would, according to contract, accrue through non-clearance within the stipulated period.

label: text
text: In an interview by the "Wah Tsz Yat Po," a leading merchant explained that there were over one hundred and forty firms which imported piecegoods, or incident, for account of native dealers. Old established firms might be able to help by extending the period for effecting delivery but some of the juniors might not be able to do so.

label: text

A number of gentlemen were taking steps to avert a crisis, these steps being similar to those adopted when danger threatened the yarn trade some years ago. A European expert with over twenty years' experience in the local piecegoods trade had approached the Hon. Mr. P. H. Holyoak (chairman of the Chamber of Commerce), says the article, and Mr. Holyoak was very sympathetic.
It is hoped that a certain amount of give and take will help materially to tide matters over and with the collaboration of the banks, hopes are entertained that a solution will be forthcoming.
That the matter is one of extreme urgency is revealed in the attitude of the native bankers some of whom are stated to be pressing dealers for the payment of advances.

"PARROTS BEAK" GANG
FOILED.

label: text
text: LOCAL VESSELS' ESCAPE.

label: text
text: “Parrot's Beak,” already notorious in the annals of Canton River piracy, has been the scene of another attempt to molest two Hongkong vessels. Fortunately, the attack was frustrated, and two pirates are believed to have met their doom, after being shot and falling into the river.

label: text
text: Five days ago a steam launched an empty lighter out of Hongkong, bound for Wuchow, where it was to pick up a cargo of firewood.

label: text
text: Near “Parrot’s Beak” in the Heungshan district three particularly long rowing boats, capable of very fast speed, approached the two vessels. In each of the boats were between ten and twenty pirates most of whom were brandishing firearms of all kinds.

label: text
text: Going alongside the lighter, the pirates attempted to clamber on deck but were frustrated through the lighter being empty and, therefore, standing high out of the water. The gang made several efforts to board the lighter. Meanwhile the coxswain of the launch had ordered his crew to open fire. Returning the fire, the pirates made off as fast as they could with the launch steaming away in the other direction.

label: text
text: The coxswain reports that he noticed two pirates fall into the water as though they had been shot.
